# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 4

**1** Brothers and sisters, I received another vision twenty days after the previous one — a prefiguring of the tribulation that is to come. **2** I was walking along a country road, about ten stades from the main road. The terrain is very hard to traverse. **3** As I walked alone, I asked the Lord to complete all the revelations and visions he had shown me through his holy church — to strengthen me and to grant repentance to all his servants who had stumbled — so that his great and glorious name might be glorified, since he had thought me worthy to show me his wonders. **4** While I was glorifying him and giving thanks, something like a voice replied to me: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." I began to wonder within myself: "How could I be double-minded, after the Lord has established me and I have seen such glorious things?" **5** A little further on, brothers and sisters — behold, I saw dust rising up as though to the heavens, and I said to myself, "Is a herd of cattle coming, stirring up a cloud of dust?" But it was about a stade away from me. **6** As the dust rose higher and higher, I began to suspect that it was something supernatural. The sun came out a little, and behold I saw before me a great beast like a massive sea-monster, and fiery locusts were pouring out of its mouth. The beast was about a hundred cubits tall and its head was like a ceramic jar. **7** I began to weep and to beg the Lord to rescue me from it. Then I recalled the word that I had heard: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." **8** So, brothers and sisters — clothed in faith in the Lord, and calling to mind the great and glorious things he had taught me — I took courage and faced the beast. The beast was charging with such rush and power that it could have devastated an entire city. **9** I drew close to it, and the great beast stretched itself flat on the ground and did nothing but stick out its tongue; it lay completely still until I had passed it. **10** Now the beast had four colors on its head: black, then fiery red mixed with blood, then gold, then white.

---

*LOGOS note: "sea-monster" for Greek ketos; "cubits" for pechys as ancient measurement; "ceramic jar" for earthenware vessel.*
